newsitem.title: UK: Rock legends to play Monserrat aid gig in London.
newsitem.headline: Rock legends to play Monserrat aid gig in London.

text.p: Some of rock music's biggest stars will perform at a benefit concert in London on September 11 to raise money for the volcano-ravaged Caribbean island of Montserrat, the Evening Standard newspaper reported on Wednesday.
Eric Clapton, Elton John, former Beatle Paul McCartney, Sting and Dire Straits' frontman Mark Knopfler have agreed to perform, the newspaper said.
Beatles producer George Martin, who has a luxury home on the island, is organising the concert at London's Royal Albert Hall and hopes to raise at least 500,000 pounds ($800,000).

Montserrat, a tiny British territory in the eastern Caribbean, has been devastated by natural disasters over the past decade. Its population has dwindled to around 5,800 from about 11,000 two years ago.
Recent volcano eruptions, the most serious on June 25, have killed about 20 residents, including Martin's maid Felina, and left hundreds homeless.

The British Geological Survey said the Soufriere Hills volcano would remain active, although without a drastic eruption, for between one and five years which local officials fear will leave the south side of the island unusable.

The British government said they were drawing up an aid package including financial assistance for those who wish to stay on the north side of Montserrat and resettlement grants for those who want to move to neighbouring islands.
